sourcedFrom: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 (2016)
cleanIntro: A big-bore Rough Rider is a transfer-bar single action and it cleans with the cylinder out and nothing else apart — Heritage says "No further disassembly is recommended" in as many words. ⛔ Three things here are Heritage's own and not generic cowboy-gun advice: the hammer goes to HALF-COCK to free the cylinder (not full cock); the BASE PIN PLUNGER at the tip of the base pin is called out by name as a thing that must be cleaned on the big-bore guns specifically; and ⛔ DRY FIRING THIS REVOLVER VOIDS THE WARRANTY.

steps.title: Hammer to HALF-COCK — that is what frees the cylinder
steps.action: Point the revolver in a safe direction, keep your finger off the trigger, and draw the hammer back to the half-cock position. You can hear the click. The cylinder will then turn freely.
steps.prose: Half-cock, not full cock. On this action the middle notch is the loading/unloading position; going all the way to full cock puts a live hammer over the trigger for no reason.
steps.quote: Pull the hammer back to the half-cock position. You can hear this click if you listen carefully (see fig. #2). Your cylinder will turn freely.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 1. UNLOADING, printed p.2

steps.title: Gate open, every chamber ejected and looked at
steps.action: Open the loading gate to expose the chambers, line each chamber up with the ejector rod and push the cartridge out, then rotate to the next. Go round the whole cylinder and then check again.
steps.prose: Six chambers, one at a time, and the second look is the one that matters — a case head in a dark chamber is easy to miss and easy to feel.
steps.quote: Open the loading gate to expose the chambers. Line up the chamber with the ejector rod and push out the cartridge. Line up the next chamber and repeat this until all chambers are unloaded. Be sure to double check that all chambers are empty.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 1. UNLOADING, printed p.2
steps.warn: Do not eject unfired cartridges onto any surface where the cartridge primer might strike a solid object. This can cause the cartridge to discharge.

steps.title: ⛔ If it will not unload, STOP — this one is Heritage's
steps.action: If the cylinder will not turn, the gate will not open, or a case will not eject: stop. Keep it pointed somewhere safe, lower the hammer to rest, and take it to a gunsmith rather than working at it.
steps.prose: ⛔ Heritage prints this as its own warning, and it is worth taking literally on a loaded single action. A gun that will not unload is a gun with something mechanically wrong holding live rounds.
steps.quote: If you experience difficulty in unloading your Rough Rider, STOP!
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 1. UNLOADING, printed p.2
steps.warn: Make certain that your revolver is pointed in a safe direction and slowly lower the hammer to the resting position. Take your Rough Rider to a competent gunsmith.

steps.title: Decocking, if the hammer is already back
steps.action: Both hands dry and unimpeded. Draw the hammer fully back with your thumb and HOLD it there while you pull the trigger. Keeping the trigger back, lower the hammer slowly past the half-cock notch — then release the trigger forward, take your finger out of the guard, and lower the hammer the rest of the way to rest.
steps.prose: ⛔ Note the order Heritage gives: the trigger is released once you are PAST the half-cock notch, not before. Release it early and the hammer catches at half-cock, which is the one place Heritage says a revolver must never be left.
steps.quote: While holding the trigger back, SLOWLY lower the hammer downward past its half-cock position.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 6. DE-COCKING OR UN-COCKING YOUR REVOLVER, printed p.4
steps.warn: Use extreme caution and care when attempting to de-cock your revolver. If your thumb slips during the process, an accidental discharge can occur, causing injury or damage to property.

steps.title: Base pin out with the lock nut held down
steps.action: With the gate open and the hammer at half-cock, depress the base pin lock nut assembly and slide the base pin all the way out while keeping the lock nut held down.
steps.prose: The lock nut has to stay depressed for the whole travel of the pin. Letting it up part-way is what makes the pin bind and what makes people start pulling harder than they should.
steps.quote: Depress the base pin lock nut assembly and slide the base pin all the way out while holding the base pin lock nut assembly down.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Cylinder out toward the loading gate — do not force it
steps.action: Take the cylinder out toward the loading-gate side of the frame. It is a deliberately close fit; ease it, do not force it in any direction.
steps.prose: ⛔ Heritage says the fit is precise on purpose. Forcing a tight cylinder sideways is how the crane-less frame window gets marked and how the cylinder ends up dragging afterwards.
steps.quote: The cylinder is designed to fit your revolver precisely, and it can be removed and replaced easily. Be careful! It is a close fit, so don't force it to move in any direction.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ NOT a steel rod — wood, aluminium or brass
steps.action: Use a wood, aluminium or brass cleaning rod and a brass bristle brush or a patch sized to the calibre. Not a steel rod.
steps.prose: ⛔ This is specified by the manufacturer, not preference. A steel rod in a soft-steel bore, run from the muzzle as this gun requires, scores the crown — and on a fixed-sight revolver the crown is your accuracy.
steps.quote: Use a wood, aluminum or brass cleaning rod (not steel) as well as a brass bristle brush or cleaning patch that is appropriate for your revolver's caliber.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5

steps.title: Bore, every chamber, and the firing pin area
steps.action: Solvent through the bore, through each of the six chambers, and around the firing pin area. ⛔ Always push the brush all the way through — never reverse direction while the brush is inside the bore or a chamber.
steps.prose: The firing pin area is named explicitly and is the one people skip: unburnt powder packs into the recess behind the frame and eventually cushions the pin.
steps.quote: Use a good quality cleaning solution to swab the bore, each chamber of your cylinder and firing pin area. While swabbing the bore, always brush all the way through the bore; never try to reverse the direction while the brush is actually in the barrel or chamber.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ The base pin plunger — named for the big-bore guns
steps.action: Clean the base pin plunger at the tip of the base pin.
steps.prose: ⛔ Heritage calls this out specifically for the big-bore revolvers and gives the reason: it is what causes returns and malfunctions. A fouled plunger means the base pin does not lock, and an unlocked base pin on a single action is a cylinder that can walk forward under recoil.
steps.quote: It is also necessary to clean the base pin plunger at the tip of the base pin on the big-bore revolvers to prevent unnecessary returns or malfunctions.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5

steps.title: Patches until clean, then light oil everywhere
steps.action: Run clean patches through the bore and chambers until they come out clean, then oil the whole revolver lightly — including the inside of the barrel — to keep rust off.
steps.prose: Lightly is the operative word and Heritage gives the reason: too much oil attracts dirt and dust, and a single action has a lot of open frame for it to get into.
steps.quote: After swabbing, run clean patches through the bore and chambers until they come out clean. Then completely, but lightly, oil the entire revolver including the inside of the barrel to prevent rust.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5
steps.warn: Firing a revolver with oil, grease or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may result in damage to the revolver and serious injury to the user or those nearby.

steps.title: ⛔ That is the end — no further disassembly
steps.action: Base pin back in, cylinder back in through the gate side, and check the base pin has locked. Heritage's published procedure stops here.
steps.prose: ⛔ Test the lock rather than assuming it: depress the base pin lock nut assembly and let it go — it should move freely and spring back on its own. If it does not, the plunger you just cleaned is not seated.
steps.quote: When you re-install the base pin, make sure it is locked onto the base pin lock nut assembly. You can test this by making sure the base pin lock nut assembly is free to move when you depress it and it returns under its own spring pressure.
steps.cite: Heritage Rough Rider Single-Action Big-Bore Revolver Owner's Instruction Manual — HEROWMANBB REV.2 02/2016 — 7. CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, printed p.5

deepAbsentReason: ⛔ HERITAGE STOPS AT THE CYLINDER, IN ITS OWN WORDS: "Remove the cylinder using the following steps. No further disassembly is recommended." The manual publishes no procedure for the backstrap, the mainspring, the hammer or the trigger group, and it adds "Do not attempt to work on it yourself." A parts list and an exploded view are printed, but a parts list is an ordering aid, not a procedure — authoring a deep clean from it would be invention wearing a citation.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: ⛔ Wood, aluminium or brass rod — NEVER steel
Brush all the way through; never reverse inside the bore
Patches until clean, then a light oil film

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS (six)
tasks: Every chamber swabbed with solution, not just the bore
Chamber mouths — .357 Mag lead loads ring them
Clean patches until they come out clean

cleaning.name: FIRING PIN AREA & FRAME
tasks: Firing pin area named by Heritage — swab it
Cylinder faces and the barrel's rear face
Light oil only; too much collects dirt and dust

cleaning.name: BASE PIN
tasks: ⛔ Clean the base pin plunger at the TIP of the base pin
Wipe the pin and its bore through the cylinder
Test the lock nut springs back before shooting

reassembly: Reverse the removal: cylinder in through the loading-gate side, then the base pin.
Ease the cylinder in — it is a close fit and must not be forced in any direction.
Re-install the base pin and confirm it has locked onto the base pin lock nut assembly.
Depress the lock nut and let it go: it must move freely and return under its own spring pressure.
Check the bore is clear of patches and excess oil before any ammunition appears.
fncheck: Unloaded, gate open, all six chambers seen empty, muzzle safe. Hammer to half-cock and spin the cylinder — it should turn freely and index with distinct clicks, no drag. Close the gate. Cock fully and lower the hammer under thumb control past the half-cock notch, releasing the trigger once past it. ⛔ Do NOT dry fire to test it — Heritage voids the warranty for that. Check the base pin is fully home and its lock nut springs back, and check the bore is clear of patch material and excess oil.
